hypotheses.claim: A descending-size (FFD-like) item priority score strictly dominates ascending or random ordering for offline bin packing on heterogeneous item sizes, because placing large items first prevents the residual-fragmentation failure mode where many small bins end up with unusable gaps; adding a capacity-complement tie-break (prefer sizes near capacity/k for small k) further reduces bin count without changing the primary ordering.

next_search_advice.direction: Choose item priority score_item as a monotone decreasing-size key with a tightness tie-break: sort items primarily by descending size, and among near-equal sizes (within a small epsilon fraction of capacity) prefer items whose size is closest to a complementary fraction of bin capacity (i.e., large-residual-filling items first). This is an FFD-flavoured reordering for the offline reorder-repack template: largest-first reduces the number of residual bins, while the complement-awareness tie-break keeps sub-one-quarter leftovers packable instead of stranding them.
